chapter: After Cab: Don Redman, teaching and records
title: Doubling money: theatre dates and the Big Broadcast earnings
summary: He imagines what a band bank would have grown to, describes doubling pay and the hourly film scale, and a California tour cancelled.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I just went to the bank and got all the money, and gave everybody their money back. But in hindsight, if we had kept that up, when we started making more money we could have put in twenty dollars a week or twenty-five dollars a week, and man, we could have run a bank account up to thousands of dollars, just putting that much money in a week. Because was making... Because when we used to double

from the Cotton Club uptown, we still made our hundred dollars and our sixty-six dollars, and we could be... Because what we made at the Cotton Club was just peanuts; we were making that double. So we made a hundred and sixty-six dollars that week! And when we made the picture, Big Broadcast of 1934, we made five hundred and some dollars in five days.
See, what they did, they made the mistake of recording as they took us, you know what I'm saying...
And that way you got ten dollars an hour.
Sure. I wonder how much they took on the recording date.

Yeah, so we got ten dollars an hour. So some days we'd make fifty dollars, the next day sixty dollars. At the end of the week, we made five hundred and some dollars. We made so much money... Evidently, Mills had a blanket amount of money for the band. We made so much money, we had to kick back about fifty dollars a piece. Because we had to take care of Mills. I mean, he's the one who... Because we hadn't ever made that kind of money before. But you can bet your bottom dollar that's the last time we made that money. Because when we went to California, the guys got to foolin' around, making mistakes,

you know, to run the time up... They canceled that tour after the first day, called the band in, called the Steel(?) band in and recorded all that Jazz -- and from then on, we made about twenty-five dollars a day, which was plenty of ...(?)...
